evidence: Clear separation into logical modules (models, services, utils, routes, templates, static) within a single 'app' package
Each module has cohesive responsibilities (e.g., services for external communication, utils for shared logic, models for data structures)
No explicit inter-process communication or service boundaries (e.g., no gRPC, REST between services, or message queues)
Single Flask application entry point (app/__init__.py, app/__main__.py) with routes.py as central routing layer
Shared dependencies across modules (e.g., utils used by services, models, routes)
No evidence of separate deployable units or containers per service (only one app directory)
Test suite is co-located with source code, testing internal modules directly
risks: Tight coupling between modules could hinder future scalability or independent deployment
Monolithic structure may become a bottleneck for large teams or high-traffic scenarios
Lack of explicit boundaries may lead to increasing technical debt over time
